title: Suspected bacterial meningitis at 72 with ampicillin already in the regimen

clinical_review.notes: Owner approved revision 2 of the M6 library-growth draft (with OpenEvidence's review).

story: A 72-year-old woman, not immunocompromised, presents with fever, headache and neck stiffness; CSF shows a neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose. Empiric vancomycin, ceftriaxone 2 g every 12 hours, ampicillin 2 g every 4 hours and dexamethasone (with or before the first antibiotic dose) are started; cultures are pending.

prescriptions.instructions: Loading dose then 15 to 20 mg/kg IV every 8 to 12 hours, pharmacy to dose
0.15 mg/kg (10 mg) IV every 6 hours, first dose with or before the first antibiotic dose

results.text: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count

reference_answer: No intervention: the empiric regimen covers Listeria (age over 50). Continue dexamethasone only if pneumococcal; narrow when cultures return.
rationale: Negative control for the Listeria rule: ampicillin in the regimen must keep it silent.

citations.supports: Empiric vancomycin, ampicillin and a third-generation cephalosporin for adults over 50; dexamethasone.
Empiric amoxicillin or ampicillin for Listeria in adults over 50.
Ampicillin or amoxicillin added with Listeria risk factors, including age over 60; checked against the WHO document 2026-11-12.
